html:
SMTO-SKL-0136 — Slack couldn't find that file

GUID: 9bc7f1bb-eff3-574c-8df1-de8c033d61dd
Slug: slack-file-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack says the file SMTO asked for doesn't exist or can't be seen by your connected Slack account. It may have been deleted. Nothing was downloaded or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list Slack files in the channel and pick the file you mean. SMTO needs the file's exact Slack ID, which the list provides.
  2. Check in Slack that the file still exists and is shared in a channel the connected account can open. Slack hides files the account can't reach, so they look missing.
  3. Ask the Agent for your request again with the file from the list. Slack didn't act on the first request, so it's safe to repeat.

What success looks like

  • The Agent finds the file and completes your request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with a link to the file copied from Slack, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack returned file_not_found for the supplied file_id under the selected workspace principal.

What this means

  • Slack returns the file_not_found API reason. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns the file_not_found API reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact file_id and visibility using the same principal.

How to fix it

  • Resolve an accessible exact file_id with slack.files (optionally filtered by channel_id or user_id) under the intended workspace_ref, and confirm the principal can see the conversation the file was shared in.
  • Use slack.files to find an accessible exact file_id under the selected principal.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended accessible file is resolved through supported file discovery.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
